title: Choose the visual world for the Event Ticketing web app (bolder hand)
question: Bolder re-roll: foreign forms at full commitment. The first dealt world leads. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll again.

options.label: Season Folio
options.lineage: botanical folios that follow one plant through its seasons
options.thesis: Every booking is one specimen drawn through its life stages on fixed-scale plates, bud to fruit to husk.
options.viewport: Top nav and search; event list as specimen captions; the open booking shown as five registered stage plates on one baseline, current stage in full colour.
options.risk: Sits near the cream-and-serif default; must hold to herbarium white and saturated fruit, and attendees do not identify with botany.

raised.raise: Booking and ticket state is a mark in a fixed cell: filled holds, hollow does not, scarlet strikes, green confirms.

options.label: Low-Res Proof
options.lineage: Emigre bitmap type specimens and 90s club flyers
options.thesis: Unresolved things render in pixels; a booking's status sharpens into smooth type the moment the saga resolves.
options.viewport: Top nav; tonight's lead event set in poster-scale pixel type; a dense event table below; bookings rail with pending states in bitmap and settled ones in smooth bold.
options.case: Beats the leader on both axes: club and gig culture is the audience's own print world, and bitmap-versus-smooth makes async state legible at a glance.
options.risk: Pixel type must stay at display sizes and status words; at body sizes it hurts reading.

options.label: Saga Line
options.lineage: metro diagrams fired as enamel station murals
options.thesis: A booking is a journey on a line: stations are states, and the payment-failed compensation path is a branch line to Refunded.
options.viewport: Midnight-blue top bar; event list coded by category line colour; the open booking drawn as a line diagram with the current station lit and the refund branch shown dim.
options.case: Beats the leader on both axes: everyone rides the metro to get to an event, and the saga literally is a branching route.
options.risk: The diagram must stay one strip per booking; drawn as a full network map it becomes decoration.

options.label: Mixtape J-Card
options.thesis: An event's sessions are a tracklist ruled in ballpoint, timed to fill the venue's capacity like a side of tape.
options.viewport: Event page as an unfolded J-card: spine title, sessions as side A and side B with right-aligned times, a capacity meter like remaining tape.
options.case: Holds audience identification (music people) but loses product clarity: hand lettering in a payment flow reads unserious.
options.risk: Handwriting at UI sizes undermines trust at checkout.

options.label: Timetable Slide Rack
options.lineage: 1970s pocket airline timetables on a light table
options.thesis: One type size; rank carried by weight, case and reversal on raked glass slides.
options.viewport: A raked rack of event slides travelling sideways.
options.case: Loses both axes: raked containers and lateral travel fight a booking task.
options.risk: Raked layout breaks forms and tables.
options.kept: State as a mark in a fixed cell.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A ticket marketplace as Eventbrite or Tixr ship it, at full craft.
canonCard.viewport: Search hero, photo event cards in a grid, sticky checkout summary.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from the competition by design.
